neutral_facts.value: The accused enticed the victim, wrongfully confined her, and had sexual intercourse with her. The victim was 19 years old at the time of the incident and voluntarily left her home to get married to the accused. She willingly became intimate with the accused on multiple occasions and made no complaints. The victim proceeded with the accused to get married in court but was apprehended by the police. The prosecution alleged that the accused made a false promise of marriage, but the court found that the victim's consent was not obtained under a misconception of fact. The accused was initially convicted, but the conviction was set aside due to insufficient evidence of a false promise.

quotes.text: The prosecutrix had left her home voluntarily, of her own free will to get married to the appellant. She was 19 years of age at the relevant time and was, hence, capable of understanding the complications and issues surrounding her marriage to the appellant.

The prosecutrix voluntarily became intimate with the appellant on a number of occasions and made no complaints to anyone. In fact, while she was proceeding with the appellant so that the two of them could get married in the court, they were apprehended by the police.

The trial court convicted the appellant under Sections 365 and 376 IPC and sentenced him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for three years under Section 365 IPC; and rigorous imprisonment for seven years under Section 376 IPC.
The prosecution case was that the appellant enticed the 19 year old daughter of PW8, wrongfully confined her and had sexual intercourse with her in lieu of his promise to marry her.
Rape is the most morally and physically reprehensible crime in a society, as it is an assault on the body, mind and privacy of the victim.

The trial court convicted the appellant under Sections 365 and 376 IPC and sentenced him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for three years under Section 365 IPC; and rigorous imprisonment for seven years under Section 376 IPC.

The court must very carefully examine whether the accused had actually wanted to marry the victim, or had mala fide motives, and had made a false promise to this effect only to satisfy his lust, as the latter falls within the ambit of cheating or deception.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The Supreme Court accepted that the prosecutrix had left her home voluntarily, of her own free will to get married to the appellant, and that she was 19 years of age and capable of understanding the complications and issues surrounding her marriage to the appellant.

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle that consent must be examined for its validity, distinguishing between rape and consensual sex, and emphasized the need to determine if the accused had mala fide intentions.

quotes.text: An accused can be convicted for rape only if his intention was mala fide, and he had clandestine motives.

There is a clear distinction between rape and consensual sex and in a case like this, the court must very carefully examine whether the accused had actually wanted to marry the victim, or had mala fide motives.
